'''Robert Douglas Brown''' (born September 24, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who is the director of player development for the [[Cal State Fullerton Titans men's basketball|Cal State Fullerton Titans men's basketball team]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=2}}, he played the [[point guard]] position.

After graduating from Cal State Fullerton, Brown entered the [[2007 NBA draft]], but went [[undrafted]]. In his first pro season, he played overseas with the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German League]] team [[Alba Berlin]], and in 2008, he returned to the United States, where he played for several NBA teams, including the [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], and the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].

While playing for [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] in the 2012–14 season, Brown tied a [[EuroLeague records since the 2000–01 season|EuroLeague scoring record since the 2000–01 season]], with 41 points (the all-time EuroLeague single-game scoring record is 99 points, held by [[Radivoj Korać]]).<ref>{{cite web|first=Vladimir|last=Stankovic|title=Radivoj Korac's 99 points|url=http://www.euroleague.net/features/voices/2010-2011/vladimir-stankovic/i/81292/radivoj-korac-s-99-points|work=EuroLeague.net|date=January 12, 2011|access-date=January 12, 2011}}</ref> Brown won the EuroLeague's [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]] in 2013.

==High school==
Brown attended [[Westchester High School (Los Angeles)|Westchester High School]], in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], where he played high school basketball. He played alongside future [[NBA]] players [[Trevor Ariza]] and [[Hassan Adams]].<ref name="fanhouseinterview">{{cite web|first=Nate|last=Jones|title=An Interview With NBA Draft Prospect Bobby Brown|url=http://www.fanhouse.com/2007/06/06/an-interview-with-nba-draft-prospect-bobby-brown/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829161521/http://www.fanhouse.com/2007/06/06/an-interview-with-nba-draft-prospect-bobby-brown/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 29, 2008|work=FanHouse.com|date=June 6, 2007|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref>

==College career==
After high school, he went on to play [[NCAA Division I]] [[college basketball]] at [[California State University, Fullerton]], where he played with the [[Cal State Fullerton Titans men's basketball|Cal State Fullerton Titans]], from 2003 to 2007. Brown was selected to the All-[[Big West Conference]] First Team, of the 2005–06 season. In his 4 years with the Titans, he scored 1,961 points, in 116 games (16.9 points per game), making him the school's all-time leader in total points scored, at the time.<ref>[http://www.fullertontitans.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/records/histcarr.htm SCORING (CAREER) Points.]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Early years===
Brown left Cal State Fullerton in 2007, but ultimately went [[undrafted]] in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. He signed with the [[Germany|German]] team [[ALBA Berlin]] in August 2007,<ref>{{cite web|title=Alba Berlin signs rookie guard Brown|url=http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14950/448/item|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080827161146/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14950/448/item|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 27, 2008|work=ULEBCup.com|date=August 28, 2008|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref> whom he helped win the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German national domestic league]].<ref name="kingssigning">{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Stein|title=New addition: Sources say Kings agree to deal with Brown|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3502700|work=ESPN.com|date=July 23, 2008|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref> He was also a participant in a five-[[overtime (sports)|overtime]] [[European professional club basketball pyramid|European second-tier level]] [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] game, in which he top-scored with 44 points, the second-highest total ever in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alba Berlin vs. KK Bosna game report|url=http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/competition/results/showgame/report?gamecode=110|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312080121/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/competition/results/showgame/report?gamecode=110|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 12, 2008|work=ULEBCup.com|date=March 12, 2008|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref>

===First NBA stint===
In 2008, Brown returned to the U.S., and played for the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in the [[NBA Summer League]], with his highlight being a game-winning shot against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], in a 77–75 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brown lifts Hornets past Bobcats|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?page=080713-Recap1|work=ESPN.com|date=July 13, 2008|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref> He was rewarded for his stellar summer league play, by his being offered a two-year contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]], one of a handful of NBA teams that courted him.<ref name="kingssigning" /> He was also pursued by multiple overseas teams that had offered him lucrative deals, among them the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli league]]'s [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref name="kingssigning" /> He also came close to accepting a multi-year contract, "in the millions", from the [[Liga ACB|Spanish league]]'s [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].<ref name="kingssigning" />

On February 19, 2009, Brown was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with [[Shelden Williams]], in exchange for [[Rashad McCants]] and [[Calvin Booth]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves Acquire Shelden Williams and Bobby Brown|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Acquire_Shelden_William-301404-1193.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2009|access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref> On September 9, he was traded to the [[New Orleans Hornets]], along with [[Darius Songaila]], in exchange for [[Antonio Daniels]], and a 2014 second round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=HORNETS ACQUIRE SONGAILA, BROWN FROM TIMBERWOLVES|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_songaila_brow_2009_09_09.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091216183604/http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_songaila_brow_2009_09_09.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 16, 2009|work=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2009|access-date=September 9, 2009}}</ref> On January 26, 2010, Brown was again traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], for a conditional [[2014 NBA Draft|2014]] 2nd round pick and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Clippers Acquire Bobby Brown From New Orleans in Exchange for 2014 Conditional Second Round Pick |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews100126.html |work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2010|access-date=January 26, 2010}}</ref>

In July 2010, Brown joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the 2010 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/summerleague_roster070510.html|title=Raptors Announce 2010 Las Vegas Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2010|access-date=July 5, 2010}}</ref>

===Return to Europe===
On September 22, 2010, Brown signed with the [[Polish Basketball League|Polish League]] team [[Asseco Prokom Gdynia|Asseco Prokom]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Ziller|title=Bobby Brown Signs With Poland's Asseco Prokom|url=http://www.aolnews.com/2010/09/22/bobby-brown-signs-with-polands-asseco-prokom/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130215134504/http://www.aolnews.com/2010/09/22/bobby-brown-signs-with-polands-asseco-prokom/|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 15, 2013|work=AOLNews.com|date=September 22, 2010|access-date=January 5, 2013}}</ref> but he was released in December, due to poor performances in the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=PLK: Bobby Brown opuszcza Asseco Prokom|url=http://www.kosz.sport24.pl/news/show/136949/plk/plk--bobby-brown-opuszcza-asseco-prokom/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101213211657/http://www.kosz.sport24.pl/news/show/136949/plk/plk--bobby-brown-opuszcza-asseco-prokom/|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 13, 2010|work=Kosz.sport24.pl|date=November 30, 2010|access-date=January 5, 2013|language=pl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Asseco Prokom, Brown part ways|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/79610/180/asseco-prokom-brown-part-ways|work=EuroLeague.net|date=December 1, 2010|access-date=January 5, 2013}}</ref> In his first EuroLeague season, he averaged 10.7 points in 26 minutes per game, over six games, with Asseco Prokom, but shot only .333 percent from the field. On December 3, 2010, he signed a two-month contract with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Aris BC|Aris]], in order to replace [[Pierre Pierce]], who was sidelined for two months with an injury.<ref>{{cite web|first=Vassilis|last=Skountis|title=Aris BSA 2003 brings in Bobby Brown |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/79726/3735|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018044852/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/79726/3735|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 18, 2012|work=EurocupBasketball.com|date=December 3, 2010|access-date=January 5, 2013}}</ref> In 35 games, he averaged 12.2 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 0.8 steals in 28.7 minutes.<ref name="EuroStats">{{cite web|title=Bobby Brown Europe Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/euro/players/bobby-brown-1.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 16, 2016}}</ref>

On August 5, 2011, Brown signed with the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German League]] team [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bobby Brown lenkt Baskets-Spiel|url=http://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/newsarchiv/2011/bobby-brown-lenkt-baskets-spiel/|work=EasyCredit-BBL.de|date=August 5, 2011|access-date=January 5, 2013|language=de}}</ref>

===Montepaschi Siena===
On August 8, 2012, Brown signed a one-year contract with the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] team [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]]. He replaced [[Euroleague 2011-12|2011–12]] Alphonso Ford top scoring trophy winner [[Bo McCalebb]], who joined [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]] a week before.<ref>{{cite web|title=MONTEPASCHI inks playmaker Brown|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/99089/7224/montepaschi-inks-playmaker-brown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703175803/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/99089/7224/montepaschi-inks-playmaker-brown|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 3, 2013|work=EuroLeague.net|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=January 5, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mens Sana Siena officially signs Bobby Brown|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/94300/mens-sana-siena-officially-signs-bobby-brown.html|work=Sportando.com|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=January 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220184215/http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/94300/mens-sana-siena-officially-signs-bobby-brown.html|archive-date=December 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He won the [[2012-13 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2012–13]] [[Alphonso Ford EuroLeague Top Scorer Trophy]], averaging 18.8 points per game. He was also fourth in the EuroLeague in assists, with an average of 5.3 per game, and led the league in several other parameters.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brown, Bobby 2012–13 Season|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000129&seasoncode=E2012|work=EuroLeague.net|access-date=April 26, 2013}}</ref>

On January 4, 2013, Brown scored 41 points in a 98–92 comeback win over [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]]. He tied the [[EuroLeague records since the 2000–01 season|EuroLeague's single-game scoring record since the 2000–01 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Siena's Brown ties Euroleague's all-time scoring mark with 41 points!|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/106736/180|work=EuroLeague.net|date=January 4, 2013|access-date=January 5, 2013}}</ref> He was eventually named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month]] for January.<ref>{{cite web|title=bwin MVP for January: Bobby Brown, Montepaschi Siena|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/108225/180|work=Euroleague.net|date=January 28, 2013|access-date=January 28, 2013}}</ref> In April 2013, Brown won the [[EuroLeague]] [[Alphonso Ford Trophy]], the annual award given to the EuroLeague's "Best Scorer" of the season. He averaged 18.8 points, 5.3 assists, and 1.7 rebounds per game, over a total of 24 games during the [[2012-13 Euroleague|2012–13 season]], while shooting .411 from the field. He scored in double figures in 22 games, reached the 20-point mark on 10 occasions, and got to 30 points twice.<ref>{{cite web|title=Montepaschi Siena's Bobby Brown wins Alphonso Ford Top Scorer Trophy|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/112863/180|work=EuroLeague.net|date=April 30, 2013|access-date=April 30, 2013}}</ref>

===Dongguan Leopards===
In the summer of 2013, Brown signed with the [[Dongguan Leopards]] of China.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bobby Brown signs with Dongguan with an NBA clause|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/104403/bobby-brown-signs-with-dongguan-with-an-nba-clause.html|work=Sportando|date=July 31, 2013|access-date=July 31, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220184458/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/104403/bobby-brown-signs-with-dongguan-with-an-nba-clause.html|archive-date=December 20, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bobby Brown (ex Montepaschi) agreed terms with DongGuan Leopards|url=http://basketball.asia-basket.com/China/news/326691|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=July 30, 2013|access-date=July 31, 2013}}</ref> On December 27, 2013, he scored 74 points in a 137–135 overtime victory over the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bobby Brown scored 74 points in China|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/109725/bobby-brown-scored-74-points-in-china.html|work=Sportando.com|date=December 27, 2013|access-date=December 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225222834/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/109725/bobby-brown-scored-74-points-in-china.html|archive-date=December 25, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Brown had scored the second-highest number of points in a single-game in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA)'s history, being just one point shy from breaking the record of 75 points scored, that was held by [[Quincy Douby]], and which has since been eclipsed by [[Errick McCollum]]'s 82 point effort, on January 30, 2015.

On May 22, 2014, Brown extended his contract with Dongguan, for three more years.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bobby Brown signs a three-year deal with Dongguan Leopards|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/120423/bobby-brown-signs-a-three-year-deal-with-dongguan-leopards.html|work=Sportando.com|date=May 22, 2014|access-date=December 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225222945/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/120423/bobby-brown-signs-a-three-year-deal-with-dongguan-leopards.html|archive-date=December 25, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Beşiktaş Sompo Japan===
On March 28, 2016, Brown signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Sompo Japan]] of Turkey, for the rest of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]]'s [[2015–16 Turkish Basketball Super League|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bobby Brown Beşiktaş Sompo Japan'da|url=http://www.bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/66004/bobby_brown_besiktas_sompo_japan_da.html|access-date=March 28, 2016|work=BJK.com.tr|date=March 28, 2016|language=tr}}</ref>

===Return to the NBA===
On September 23, 2016, Brown signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-announce-training-camp-roster|title=Rockets Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2016|access-date=September 23, 2016}}</ref> On December 5, 2016, he was waived by the Rockets after appearing in six games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-bringing-back-Donatas-Motiejunas-10695779.php|title=Rockets bringing back Donatas Motiejunas|work=Chron.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/transactions/|title=NBA Transactions|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 12, 2016}}</ref> He re-signed with the Rockets on December 16.<ref>{{cite web|author=Houston Rockets|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/809800401964986368|title=Official: Rockets sign free agent Bobby Brown...|work=Twitter|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=December 16, 2016}}</ref>

On September 25, 2017, Brown re-signed with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/training-camp-roster|title=Rockets Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=September 25, 2017}}</ref> On January 5, 2018, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|last=Feigen|first=Jonathan|url=http://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-to-waive-Bobby-Brown-keep-Gerald-Green-12475214.php|title=Rockets to waive Bobby Brown, keep Gerald Green|work=chron.com|date=January 5, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2018}}</ref>

===Olympiacos Piraeus===
On February 22, 2018, Brown signed with [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] of Greece, for the rest of the [[Greek Basket League]] and [[EuroLeague]] seasons.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8jycjc87ifqn5wtv/olympiacos-adds-former-ford-trophy-winner-brown Olympiacos adds former Ford Trophy winner Brown.]</ref>

===Mornar===
On November 1, 2018, Brown signed a one-year contract with [[KK Mornar|Mornar]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Former EuroLeague top scorer is coming to ABA – Bobby Brown pens deal with Mornar |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=40873 |website=aba-liga.com |access-date=2 November 2018}}</ref> On November 28, Brown parted ways with [[KK Mornar|Mornar]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mornar have a new point guard – Brown OUT, Grant IN |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=41076 |website=aba-liga.com}}</ref>

===NBA G League Ignite===
On February 1, 2021, Brown signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/nba-g-league-ignite-roster|title=NBA G League Ignite Roster|date=February 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=April 28, 2021}}</ref>

==The Basketball Tournament==
Brown played for the CitiTeam Blazers in the [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|2018]] edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT), a single-elimination winner-take-all tournament for a $2 million prize. In two games, he averaged a team-high 20.5 points per game, 3.5 rebounds per game and 3.0 assists per game. CitiTeam Blazers lost in the second to Team Challenge ALS. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|TBT 2019]], Brown played for four-time defending champion [[Overseas Elite]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/teams/overseas-elite-0 |title=Overseas Elite |website=thetournament.com |date=2019 |access-date=August 4, 2019 |archive-date=August 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802011705/http://thetournament.com/teams/overseas-elite-0 |url-status=dead }}</ref> who advanced to the semifinals where they suffered their first-ever defeat, losing to Carmen's Crew, 71–66.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |title=#1 Carmen's Crew 71, #1 Overseas Elite 66 |website=thetournament.com |date=August 4, 2019 |access-date=August 4, 2019 |archive-date=January 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200123041911/http://www.thetournament.com/news/1-carmens-crew-71-1-overseas-elite-66 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==National team career==
Brown represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]], where he won a bronze medal.

==Post-playing career==
On July 31, 2023, Brown was announced as the director of player development for the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball team]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bobby Brown, Former NBA Player, Joins CSUN Men’s Basketball Staff as Director of Player Development |url=https://bvmsports.com/2023/07/31/bobby-brown-former-nba-player-joins-csun-mens-basketball-staff-as-director-of-player-development/ |website=BVM Sports |access-date=January 15, 2024 |date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brown shares the same name with the [[Bobby Brown|famous American R&B singer]]. In an interview, he affirmed jokes about his name: "Someone is always trying to be funny...asking me where [[Whitney Houston|Whitney]]'s at."<ref name="fanhouseinterview" /> Upon announcing his signing with the [[Sacramento Kings|Kings]], [[ESPN]] ran the headlines "Their prerogative: Kings agree with Bobby Brown", and "New addition: Sources say Kings agree to deal with Brown",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/keyword/search?searchString=Bobby+Brown&page=espn|title=ESPN search results for Bobby Brown|work=ESPN.com|access-date=November 12, 2016}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Note: This search yields the same article as the "New addition..", but with a variant title, "Their prerogative: Kings agree with Bobby Brown</ref> in reference to the singer's 1988 anthem "[[My Prerogative]]", and his former [[boy band]] [[New Edition]], respectively.
